title: Graphical glitches all over the place in both game and editor after Nvidia driver update
body: Since updating to the latest Nvidia drivers, I get moving graphical glitches in both my games and the Godot editor. Pixels jump along the X axis when I pan or move the camera. Nearest filtering makes the problem visible, while linear filtering hides it in many cases, and shaders are affected too. I tested Godot 4.3, 4.4 beta 1, and 4.4 beta 2 with Forward+ on Windows 11, Nvidia driver 572.16, and a GeForce 30-series GPU. An empty project with the default sprite reproduces it.

symptoms_visible: I see graphical artifacts in both the Godot editor and my games; pixel columns jump along the X axis as I pan or move the camera.
Nearest filtering makes the artifacts easy to see, while linear filtering hides them in many cases, and shaders can show them too.
N0.label: N0 moving rendering artifacts reported

symptoms_visible: The moving pixel glitches continue with Nvidia image sharpening disabled globally and explicitly disabled for Godot.
N1_x.label: N1_x sharpening-setting aftermath

symptoms_visible: The artifacts remain in Godot's Vulkan-based Forward+ and Mobile renderers on the newer driver.
The same scenes display normally after rolling back the Nvidia driver or when using Direct3D 12.
N2.label: N2 driver and API isolation established

symptoms_visible: The pixel corruption is still present on the affected Nvidia driver when Godot uses Vulkan.
N3.label: N3 Nvidia regression acknowledged

symptoms_visible: After updating to Nvidia driver 572.60, the glitches and artifacts are no longer present in Godot using Vulkan Forward+.
N_terminal.label: terminal artifacts gone after Nvidia update

symptoms_visible: After updating to Nvidia driver 572.60, the glitches and artifacts are no longer present in Godot using Vulkan Forward+.
N_terminal_shortcut.label: terminal shortcut to corrected Nvidia driver

solution.intent: Treat the artifacts as Nvidia image sharpening or contrast enhancement being enabled for Godot and disable that driver setting.
solution.concrete_example: Open Nvidia Control Panel, check the global and Godot-specific 3D settings, and disable image sharpening or any similar contrast-enhancement option.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's system; c0-c4. The maintainer suggested checking image sharpening based on an older AMD case. The reporter verified that the sole sharpening option was disabled globally and in a Godot profile, but the artifacts continued.

question_patterns: Can you show the relevant Nvidia Control Panel settings for Godot?
Could you confirm whether any other sharpening option is enabled and attach a screenshot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There is only one sharpening setting, and it is disabled both globally and in the profile I created for Godot. Here is my Nvidia Control Panel screenshot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Image sharpening was enabled for Godot, and turning it off immediately removed every artifact.

question_patterns: If you temporarily roll back to an earlier Nvidia driver, what happens?
Can you test an older driver and report whether the same project still glitches?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rolled back to 566.36 and the artifacts disappeared. The same Godot projects display normally on that driver.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The artifacts are identical on 566.36 and on the latest driver.
A different pre-update Nvidia driver also displays the project correctly.

question_patterns: Does the problem reproduce if Godot uses a different rendering API?
Can you compare Vulkan with Direct3D 12 on the same machine and project?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With Vulkan, Forward+ and Mobile show the issue. Using Direct3D 12 on the same system, I do not see the artifacts.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The exact same corruption appears with Direct3D 12, Vulkan, and Compatibility rendering.

question_patterns: Is Godot the only application where you can reproduce this?
Do any other Vulkan applications show similar corruption on this driver?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is not limited to Godot. I can see similar visual glitches in Doom + Doom II using Vulkan, and there are many matching reports from other Vulkan applications.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every other Vulkan application works normally, and only one specific Godot project is affected.

edges.comment: c4-c8 and c18-c24, folding affected Windows/Nvidia users into one simulated user side. The sharpening screenshot is the opening reporter's. Rollback, Direct3D 12, cross-application Vulkan behavior, and additional GPU reports came from other affected users and establish the same driver-level chain; the unrelated Ubuntu Transparent BG report in c11-c15 is excluded.

question_patterns: Did Nvidia respond to your report or acknowledge a matching problem?
What does Nvidia's official feedback thread say about these artifacts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reported it to Nvidia and linked this issue. Nvidia support directed me to its official driver feedback thread, whose opening post now lists an internal bug for minor rendering artifacts in Godot and other Vulkan applications with the affected driver.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Nvidia could not reproduce any driver issue, and its feedback thread has no matching Vulkan reports.
Nvidia acknowledged the same rendering artifacts under a different internal tracking number.

edges.comment: c7-c10 and c26. The opening reporter filed the Nvidia report, and the official feedback thread subsequently acknowledged matching Godot/Vulkan artifacts. Later comments established that intermediate hotfix drivers could still exhibit the issue.

solution.intent: Treat this as an Nvidia driver regression rather than a Godot rendering bug: update to an Nvidia driver containing the vendor fix, then verify Godot under Vulkan; until then, roll back the driver or use Direct3D 12 as a temporary workaround.
solution.concrete_example: Install Nvidia driver 572.60 or a newer fixed driver and retest the same project with Vulkan Forward+. Affected users confirmed that 572.60 removed the artifacts. If updating is not yet possible, use 566.36 or configure rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows to d3d12 temporarily.
solution.inference_hint: The combined rollback, API comparison, cross-application reports, and Nvidia acknowledgment support the final diagnosis that this is an Nvidia-side Vulkan presentation regression. The conclusion that Godot should not blacklist drivers or carry an engine mitigation is maintainer reasoning, not a fact supplied by the opening reporter.

edges.comment: c26-c42. Nvidia fixed the reported image corruption in 572.60; affected user DizzasterDev verified Vulkan Forward+ without artifacts in c32, and further affected users confirmed the correction in c35-c37. These affected users are folded into the simulated user side. The final driver retest is terminal-side evidence, not required upstream evidence.

solution.intent: Recognize the temporal link to the Nvidia update as a likely vendor driver regression, recommend moving to a vendor-fixed driver and verifying the same Vulkan scene, with rollback or Direct3D 12 only as temporary alternatives.
solution.concrete_example: This started immediately after the Nvidia update and reproduces in an empty project across several Godot versions, so update to Nvidia's corrected driver and retest. If the corrected driver is not available yet, temporarily roll back or use Direct3D 12 instead of Vulkan.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut permits the final correct direction directly from the opening report, while recognizing that the stronger driver/API isolation and Nvidia acknowledgment were collected later.

edges.comment: Answer-key shortcut required because the first real thread move was the falsified sharpening hypothesis. The terminal confirmation comes from affected users who later installed the corrected Nvidia driver; it is not assumed to have been known by the opening reporter at N0.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as an Nvidia driver regression affecting Vulkan rendering or presentation, not a texture-filtering defect in Godot.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the issue began after the Nvidia update, disappears on rollback, is absent with Direct3D 12, affects other Vulkan applications, and was acknowledged by Nvidia.
Must not settle on Nvidia image sharpening or contrast enhancement as the cause; it was disabled globally and for Godot while the artifacts continued.
Must recommend updating to an Nvidia driver containing the vendor fix; driver rollback or Direct3D 12 may be offered only as temporary workarounds, not as the underlying fix.
Must not require a Godot-side driver blacklist or engine mitigation as the resolution, since the accepted thread conclusion is that the temporary regression was Nvidia's responsibility.
Must ask the user to verify the same Vulkan workload after installing the corrected driver before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Godot user who can compare engine versions, rendering methods, filtering modes, Nvidia profiles, and GPU driver versions; additional affected users are folded into the user side for rollback and cross-application testing.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and evidence-oriented, with short replies, screenshots, concrete configuration details, and links to the vendor report.
